# Theorem 1: an explicit epsilon_0 in the controlled regime (generated by experiments/exp_theory_t1.py)

The statements and proofs are in THEORY_T1.md.  Setting: continuum Gram, Gaussian features of the kernels' width, noiseless, equal masses, n = 1; the network is the paper's P0 unit.  `cert` is the sufficient condition of Theorem T1 (all constants explicit); eps_0 is the largest grid value from which `cert` holds at every smaller one of the grid (half decades); eps_max is the measured analogue (the network forms exactly the limit object's units from there down).  Constants of Prop. A: ball arithmetic (python-flint).  The other constants are double precision with 0.1 % margins on the quadratures.

## A. The unit (Lemma 2.1-2.3)

lambda sqrt(eps) -> c_u = pi a_max/(2 sqrt 2 G sqrt(v_s)) = 7.0248; B(s) s^3 -> 4/(G gamma^2 m) = 33.333 (the dormant coefficient at distance s from the wall, independent of eps).  `bound` is the explicit bound of Lemma 2.2 (first form), `closed` its closed form rho^{3/2}/(1 - s_e^2) (a_max eps^{3/2}/(m sqrt(2 v_s))) cos th/sin^3 th; the mass identity int W d eta = a_max^2 sinh^2 x/(2 G m) holds to the relative error in the last column.

## F. The first-order formula  eps_* = (c_u min(q_1, q_2, q_3))^2

c_u = lambda sqrt(eps) = 7.0248.  q_1 = min_j mu_j/(D_j + s_Omega) (the dormant margins against the deviation bound and the budget distance), q_2 = min_k (tau_{k+1} - tau_k)/(window_k + lead_{k+1}) (the order condition), q_3 = tau_1/(first lead); all at eps = 1e-22, where the O(eps) terms (dormant mass, centre drift) vanish.  The first-order threshold is eps_* = (c_u min(q_1, q_2, q_3))^2 (lambda mu >= D + s_Omega  <=>  sqrt(eps) <= c_u mu/(D + s_Omega)); eps_0 is the grid value.
